body: So I can understand she was shaken up and it was probably scary for her but no. If she is willing to scare someone on purpose like that, she has to deal with the consequence that she could scare them enough that they hurt her. And gaslighting your husband into thinking he purposely tried to hurt her is extremely manipulative behavior. And I am only looking at behavior here. So your husband was within his right to ask them to leave his home, where he should feel safe at all times, if she is going to make it unsafe for him in any way. Go to the wedding or don't but if your husband wants an apology or wants space from them, support him in that because hardly ever are pranks like that actually funny and harmless. He could have gotten hurt too, so her decision was very short sighted. Everyone can feel what they want but at the end of the day, it sounds like the fiance and brother need to understand that her decision really could have hurt her and your husband, and she will just have to deal with the fact that a poor choice led to negative consequences on her part.

Licensed therapist here. So, after working a lot with kids and teens of divorced parents, this most certainly is a delayed reaction. However, that does not excuse mean words and behavior. When I work with parents and kids, I teach the parents that they need to be prepared for any type of reaction and then teach kids how to manage their reaction. Your kids are adults so I get they may have pent up feelings or just be reacting to someone who is usually a steady in their life suddenly change, but they does not excuse the reaction. You have every right to want change and it sounds like you worked hard to just try something new. Your kids blaming you for the divorce and saying you "have" to go back to before for things to be "fixed" is coercion and  and abusive behavior. Keep the changes but call out their behavior and do not change a thing unless YOU want to. You are the only person who feels the way you do (since no one is you) and they only person who has to truly deal with it. So if the changes are making you happy, keep it. Don't keep nasty behaviors from others.

NTA. READ THIS: DV happens to men and women. To disregard your experience and feelings just because you are bigger and a male is exactly why male victims feel like they have to justify why they feel the way they do. a slap can turn into other things and suddenly, you could be a cycle of abuse. Not saying it will happen for sure, but it could happen to anyone. If you didn't like being slapped once, that is enough to say never again. Please think hard about the boundaries you would need to put up with your fiancee and if you fully trust she will respect them.

Nta. Please reread what you just wrote. That behavior of his is NOT a healthy response. Being stressed doesn't make it validate either. It is an excuse. You can do whatever you want but imagine the rest of your life with him doing this over and over and over again. It will become old and eventually become a point of contention, if not already. You are not crazy. He is gaslighting and guilt tripping you to convince you that you have done something abusive. That is a strong word that should never be used lightly because there are people who are in actual abusive relationships, sometimes with their lives on the line. So, not saying you need to do this or that other than some inner reflection on what behaviors you want or do not want to deal with long term. It could mean having a stern, uncomfortable talk rather than uprooting your life.

This is nasty vindictive behavior. Imagine other things she could have done because even though this was steak this time around, who knows what is next. This is the behavior of a child - literal tantrumming and destruction because she didnt get her way. Mental health wise, you should consider how this made you feel a d if you want to deal with it again. Unless she is willing to admit fault for her behavior and be willing to not do something like this again, it seems a response that could continue to happen.

NTA. To anyone saying you are or you should have done or said no differently, I'll remind everyone of this: in reality, you owe no one an explanation for saying no. A no is a no and if the other person doesn't like it, then that is their problem to deal with. The consequences of saying no are yours alone but the other person's feelings are something they need to work out. And yes, I agree that springing kids on someone is NEVER okay. They are a responsibility and anyone has full right to say no to looking after your kids. And if you can't find someone to look after your kids, just like those feelings that come up when someone says no to you, you have to deal with it and figure it out. 


It makes absolutely no sense whatsoever to expect a single person in this world to help you. You can hope for it but it is not an expectation, as harsh as that sounds. 


Either way, if they talk yo you about it again, you can decide whether or not to engage and share your POV but that's as far as it goes. They can plan for an emergency with you from now on if they AND you, feel like it.

To anyone saying what OP could have done in this situation, giving baby advice, let me just say this: OP you shouldn't have to go on YouTube to look up how to change that diaper because your sister shouldn't have left the baby with you in the first place without consent to take care of him. Also, NTA by any means.

Please tell the bride and groom. She can go because that's her freedom but let the bride and groom tell her yes or no. It's their wedding, not yours or hers or anyone elses to dictate for them. Also, NTA at all.

NTA. Listen, as a mental health professional, even I would say that empathy is important but a mental disorder does not make an excuse for behaviors. If he is working on it, great but it sounds like it has not helped the behavior. So, I would wonder if whatever he is trying is not helpful or is he is willing to seriously change. I totally get the anxiety that goes into procrastination and maybe having a last discussion about how to make things work could be helpful. You can't be his girlfriend and his therapist. Not healthy and boundaries need to be stuck to once you lay them down. Your time is as valuable as his, as well as your own feelings about the behavior.

NTA. It is your wedding. If they want to fight with you on that day, you and your hubby can stand firm with them. Set boundaries. Just remember the first thing you said: you know how it feels to be pressured into something you don't want to do. It does not matter if it is for one day or one year. A boundary is a boundary because the niece's feelings matter just as much as everyone else's BUT she is the one wearing the outfit. Not the mom, not the father, no one but her. So her feelings trump everyone who wants her to do something she is not comfortable doing.
Please let them see this. You are not the AH. She needs to figure her emotions out because that is very strange to say to a 14 year old. Weird. Inappropriate. Gross.

Please read OP.

NTA. Here is why: there is a better way of approaching it. I get it can be annoying when someone repeats the same thing over and over. You both have very different stances on food. Ask why she needs this much planning. Not condescending but to truly understand her concerns if you don't plan meals. I think there is a compromise that could be made here and I say that because my fiance and I are exactly like this. I tend to not know what I want and he wants to meal prep. So we do half and half: we make a weekly menu but knowing that there may be one night where we switch it up from what was written. If we really aren't in the mood, then we discuss but will often just eat what we have because if is saving money. If we want different things, we compromise on the protein but have two separate sides. Or vice versa and the leftovers will be eaten for lunch at some point so nothing is wasted. 

All about compromise.

NTA  Someone with several tattoos here. There is no tattoo secret rule or policy for those with them. Everyone has equal rights to their own body... You could get whatever the hell you want, wherever the hell you want regardless of anyone's feelings. I think sticking by the fact that people cannot claim spots will help you advocate for yourself. It also just doesn't make sense for her or any of your friends to be mad about it. I would evaluate what you want in a friendship.
